Detailed Subtask: Separate identity from tenancy: identity(provider+subject) -> account -> tenant. File-backed index at platform root, random stable tenant id, first sign-in provisions the directory with marker, seeded portals and a tracker header.
Description: There was no signup and no provisioning: a second person signing in got an empty directory, and the tenant id was a hash of the login, so two providers forked one person into two CVs and losing the login made the data unreachable.

Detailed Subtask: Self-service delete with typed confirmation, soft-delete plus 7-day grace, session revocation before file removal, then hard purge of directory, keys and identities; plus a zip export of the tenant directory
Description: There is no way to leave. Job-search data implies someone is exiting their employer, and GDPR erasure and portability are obligations for the EU users this will have.
Acceptance Criteria: PASS: delete revokes sessions first, refuses sign-in immediately, purges only inside tenants/{id}, removes stored keys by name, and is recoverable during the grace period; export produces a zip without key material. FAIL: purge resolves outside the tenant root, or keys survive because deletion relied on them being in the directory.
Test Cases: 1) Delete signs out every device. 2) Deleted account cannot sign back in. 3) Purge refuses a tenant id that escapes the root. 4) Keys are gone by name, not incidentally. 5) Export excludes provider-keys.json.
Security / Operational Checks: Recursive delete driven by an id is where a path bug becomes catastrophic — resolve through containedTenantDir and never take the id from a request body
Rollout Steps: Ship with export, not after: leaving without losing your work is the honest version of the isolation promise
Risk: High — an over-broad purge destroys another tenant's data irrecoverably
Notes: Implemented 2026-08-16: typed confirm, 7-day grace, named key wipe, contained rm, zip export minus provider-keys.json. Session revocation uses account.sessionVersion in withTenant (BL-034 Redis still open). Cron: node scripts/account-lifecycle.mjs purge-expired.
